title: A four-stage deployment pipeline: workspaces, rules per item type and pairing
objective_text: Create a four-stage deployment pipeline, assign a workspace that can go in each stage, add the rules each item type supports, and predict how rules, pairing and deploys behave.
scenario: The Claims team adds a UAT stage between Test and Production. The first draft has three stages, two workspaces that can't be assigned, and rules that either can't exist or change the kind of source. Omar also expects to deploy to UAT.

expected.description: Stages Development, Test, UAT, Production. Workspaces Claims-Dev, Claims-Test, Claims-UAT, Claims-Prod. Nora assigns Claims-Prod. Priya creates six rules: default lakehouse for Score claims and data source for Claims mirror in Test, UAT and Production. Notebook takes only default lakehouse, mirrored database only data source, lakehouse none. Rules apply on the next deploy and are lost on unassign. A notebook added later isn't paired, a rename doesn't unpair, Omar can't deploy to UAT, and only the notebook definition is copied.

When you unassign a workspace, you lose the stage's deployment history and configured rules.

explanation: A deployment pipeline has 2 to 10 stages, set when it's created. Each stage gets one workspace, assigned by an admin of that workspace. The workspace must be on a Fabric capacity and can't already be in another pipeline. Rules live on the later stages, never Development, and only the item's owner creates them. A notebook takes only a default lakehouse rule. A mirrored database takes only data source rules, and a data source rule keeps the same kind of source. Lakehouses take no rules. Rules apply on the next deploy and are lost when a workspace is unassigned. Items pair by name and type when a workspace is assigned or an item is deployed, so a notebook added later doesn't pair, and a rename doesn't unpair. Deploying needs a pipeline admin who's at least a contributor in both workspaces. A deploy copies definitions, not data or workspace settings.
review_notes: Checked on Learn 2026-11-23. intro-to-deployment-pipelines (last updated 2026-09-29): 2 to 10 stages, default Development, Test and Production. Lakehouse, Notebook and Mirrored database are supported items with no preview mark, while semantic models, reports, paginated reports and Power BI dataflows are marked preview. create-rules (last updated 2026-09-01): the rule table lists Dataflow gen1 (data source, parameter), Semantic model (data source, parameter), Paginated report (data source), Mirrored database (data source) and Notebook (default lakehouse), and no lakehouse. Data source rules only work between sources of the same type. You must own the item to create a rule. No rules in the development stage. Rules take effect on the next deploy to that stage. assign-pipeline (last updated 2026-11-02): you must be an admin of the workspace, the workspace isn't assigned to another pipeline and is on a Fabric capacity. Pairing is by name, type and folder when a workspace is assigned or an item deployed. A new item added later isn't paired automatically. Renaming doesn't unpair. Unassigning loses the stage's deployment history and configured rules. understand-the-deployment-process (last updated 2026-09-24): data, permissions and workspace settings aren't copied. To deploy you must be a pipeline admin and a contributor, member or admin of both workspaces.

Not graded: whether stages can be added or renamed after creation (get-started-with-deployment-pipelines, last updated 2025-12-15, contradicts itself), the Dataflow gen1, semantic model and paginated report rows of the rule table (those Power BI items deploy in preview), and folders and deployment plans (preview).
